text_blocks.snippet:
Common scams active in Central Illinois include fake text messages about unpaid vehicle tolls or driver's license penalties, deceptive online repair services overcharging for home fixes, and phone impostors posing as local law enforcement or the courts. Local authorities and the ⁠Better Business Bureau
track these threats closely.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake text messages about unpaid vehicle tolls or driver's license penalties, deceptive online repair services overcharging for home fixes, and phone impostors posing as local law enforcement or the courts

list.snippet: DMV and Toll Text Phishing: Scammers send fraudulent texts claiming to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or tollway systems, threatening license suspension or fines unless you click a link to pay.

Garage Door Impostors: Con artists set up fake search engine listings and websites pretending to be legitimate local repair companies (such as regional door services), overcharging thousands of dollars or intentionally damaging equipment.

Law Enforcement Impostors: Scammers call or leave voicemails pretending to be from local sheriff's departments or the federal courts, demanding immediate cash or digital payments to clear fake warrants.
Online Shopping and Holiday Ads: Fraudulent social media ads and replica retail sites market popular items at steep discounts, stealing credit card data without delivering any goods.
Do not click links: Never select links or scan QR codes found in unexpected text messages or social media posts regarding official state business.
Verify independently: Look up official phone numbers manually through verified directories rather than using numbers provided in voicemails or caller IDs.
Practice the pause: Take a moment to step back when faced with high-pressure demands for immediate secrecy or urgent payment.
Report suspicious activity: Utilize local educational resources or log threats directly via the BBB Scam Stop Program.
